description: Open-source AI penetration testing agent that exploit-verifies every finding. Autonomous 22-phase pentests of web apps & APIs with CVSS-scored PDF reports. Self-hosted, bring your own LLM, or run fully local with Ollama.

written.description: Runs a second, independent agent whose only job is to re-exploit what the first one claimed, so a finding is either reproduced or dropped. One self-hosted binary with a local dashboard.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(web): keep resumed wildcard inventories stable under subdomain exclusions (#937)

* fix(web): keep a resumed wildcard inventory stable under exclusion patterns

Follow-up to #934. Auto-resume rebuilds the scan config from the live
server config, so subdomain exclusion patterns added while a wildcard scan
is in flight were applied to the persisted inventory on resume. Dropping a
host the scan had already moved past shifted the saved resume index: the
next unscanned host was recorded as finished with no child scan and never
assessed, and the dropped host's child record (and its findings link) was
detached from the parent and counted as skipped.

filterExcludedSubdomains now mirrors capWildcardInventory: positions before
the resume index and hosts with a started child (id or start time) are
always kept, so only hosts the scan has not reached yet follow the current
patterns. The settings description now says so.

Tests: two resume tests drive runWildcardTarget with a shutdown at the
resume index (both fail on main), plus a unit test that covers each guard
on its own (mutation-checked).

* fix(web): keep per-scan exclusions across resume; trust the index only for a saved inventory

Review follow-ups:
- Save exclude_subdomains in the queue state and restore it on resume.
  Wildcard resume after a restart or pause rebuilds the request from the
  queue state, which kept every other scan option but not this one, so a
  scan interrupted during discovery re-ran discovery without its own
  exclusions and scanned those hosts.
- Apply the resume index and started-child guards only when the inventory
  was restored from the saved (already filtered) list. A raw discovery
  re-read is shuffled and is not the list the index points into, and a
  fresh run that lands in an older scan directory can carry stale children.
- Settings text: covers pause as well as restart, and notes that removing a
  pattern does not add back hosts already left out.

Tests: a resume case where a moved-past host has no child id, a raw
re-read case, and a queue-state round trip (each fails with its guard
removed).
